Grill or char the peppers, chillies, tomatoes, onion and garlic until blackened and soft.
Peel everything and chop finely or mash together.
Season with caraway, salt, oil and lemon juice.
Top with tuna, quartered eggs and olives and serve with bread.
Mix the tuna, capers, parsley, potato and a pinch of salt.
Spread half on one side of each pastry sheet, making a well in the middle.
Crack an egg into the well and fold the pastry over into a triangle.
Slide into hot oil and fry for 1 minute per side until crisp, keeping the yolk runny.
Drain and serve at once with lemon.
Hollow the quince halves a little more and keep them in lemon water.
Mix the beef with onion, parsley, half the cinnamon and salt and fill the quinces.
Lay in a pan with the butter, oil, saffron, remaining cinnamon, sugar and 500 ml water.
Cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the quince is tender.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until syrupy.
Rub the semolina with the olive oil and a pinch of salt, rest 30 minutes, then bring together with water into a soft dough.
Knead the date paste with cinnamon into a rope.
Flatten the dough into a log, lay the date rope inside, close it and cut into diamonds.
Fry at 170°C for 4 minutes until golden, then soak in warm honey with orange blossom water for 2 minutes.
Brew the tea with mint and sugar and serve with the makroudh.
Brown the beef and onion in the oil.
Add the tomato paste, harissa, caraway and paprika for 2 minutes.
Add the water and simmer for 40 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and vermicelli and cook for 10 minutes.
Finish with parsley and serve with lemon.
Heat the oil gently and stir in the mloukhia powder for 5 minutes without letting it catch.
Add the water little by little, whisking, and bring to a simmer.
Cook on very low heat for 2 hours, stirring often, until dark and thick.
Add the beef, tomato paste, garlic, spices, bay leaves and salt and cook for 2 hours more until the oil rises.
Brown the chicken and onion in the oil, add the tomato paste, harissa and spices.
Add 1.5 l water, the chickpeas and potatoes and simmer for 35 minutes.
Steam the pasta over the broth for 15 minutes, toss with butter and a ladle of broth and steam 10 minutes more.
Serve the pasta topped with chicken, potatoes and sauce.
Rub the lamb with ras el hanout, cinnamon, saffron and salt.
Cook with the onions and butter for 10 minutes.
Add 700 ml water, cover and simmer for 2 hours.
Add the raisins, almonds and honey and cook for 25 minutes until thick and glossy.
Brown the merguez in the oil and remove.
Soften the pepper and garlic, add the tomato paste, harissa and caraway.
Add the tomatoes and 100 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes, then return the merguez.
Crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5 minutes until set.
Cook the onions slowly in 4 tbsp oil for 25 minutes until golden.
Add the raisins, saffron, cumin, cinnamon, sugar, vinegar and 100 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes until jammy.
Fry in the remaining oil for 3 minutes per side.
Serve the fish on the onion sauce.
Fry the potatoes, pumpkin, peppers and tomatoes separately until soft and golden.
Chop everything together roughly on a board.
Mix with harissa, caraway, olive oil and salt.
Serve warm in bread or on a plate.
Fry the garlic, tomato paste, harissa and spices in the oil for 2 minutes.
Add 800 ml water and the potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer gently for 8 minutes.
Season with salt and lemon juice.
Scatter with parsley and serve with bread.
Simmer the chickpeas in their liquid with half the garlic, cumin and salt for 15 minutes.
Ladle over the hot chickpeas and broth.
Poach the eggs in the broth for 3 minutes and add one to each bowl.
Top with harissa, remaining garlic, tuna, capers, olive oil, cumin and lemon, and mix at the table.
Mix the beef, rice, onion, parsley, spices, 1 tbsp oil and salt.
Roll spoonfuls in the cabbage leaves and pack into a pot.
Mix the tomato paste and harissa with 800 ml water, the remaining oil and salt and pour over.
Weigh down with a plate, cover and simmer for 50 minutes.
Brown the beef and onion in the oil, add the garlic, tomato paste, harissa and spices.
Add 1 l water and simmer for 50 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and bulgur and stir.
Cover and cook on low for 15 minutes until the bulgur has absorbed the sauce.
Make a soft dough with the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, egg and water and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Shape into 10 small oval buns and rest 20 minutes.
Fry at 170°C for 2 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Fill with tuna, potato, egg, olives and capers.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil, add the tomato paste, harissa and caraway.
Add the tomatoes, artichokes, fava beans and 150 ml water.
Crack in the eggs, cover and cook 5 minutes.
Brown the lamb and onion in the oil, add the tomato paste, harissa and spices.
Add 2 l water and simmer for 60 minutes.
Add the carrots and potatoes for 20 minutes, then the zucchini and chickpeas for 15 minutes.
Steam the couscous over the broth twice, fluffing between, and rub in the butter and a ladle of red broth.
Serve the couscous with lamb, vegetables and broth.
Pound the garlic with the cumin and coriander to a paste.
Brown the beef in the oil, add half the paste and the tomato paste, then 700 ml water.
Add the liver, harissa and the rest of the paste and simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce is thick.
Rub the semolina with half the oil and salt, add water and knead to a soft dough, then rest 20 minutes.
Cook the onions in the remaining oil for 10 minutes, add the tomatoes, harissa, mint and caraway and cook until thick.
Divide the dough in two, roll each into a round and spread filling over one, then cover with the other and seal.
Cook in a dry heavy pan for 6 minutes per side.
Brush with butter and cut into wedges.
shiro powder (spiced chickpea and broad bean flour)
Cook the onions in a dry pot for 6 minutes.
Add the oil, garlic, tomato and berbere and cook for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the shiro powder with the water little by little to avoid lumps.
Simmer on low, stirring often, for 15 minutes until velvety.
Break the dried beef into small pieces and soak in warm water for 15 minutes.
Cook the onions in a dry pan for 8 minutes, add the butter, garlic, berbere and tomato paste for 3 minutes.
Add the beef and its soaking water and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Stir in the torn injera until it absorbs the sauce.
Soften the onions in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric and cumin for 2 minutes.
Add the carrots and potatoes with 150 ml water, cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage and salt, cover and cook for 15 minutes until everything is tender.
Sear the beef in the oil over high heat for 3 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic and peppers and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the butter, rosemary and berbere and toss for 2 minutes.
Warm the beans with a little of their liquid and mash roughly.
Fry half the onion in 2 tbsp oil with berbere and cumin for 3 minutes and stir into the beans.
Season with salt and lemon juice.
Top with the remaining onion, tomatoes, chillies, chopped egg and the rest of the oil.
Soften the onions in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and cardamom for 2 minutes.
Add the greens with 150 ml water, cover and cook for 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the chillies and salt and cook uncovered for 5 minutes until the liquid is gone.
Cook the onions in a dry pan for 10 minutes, add the oil, garlic and ginger and divide among four pots.
Misir wat: add berbere and the red lentils with 600 ml water and simmer 25 minutes.
Kik alicha: add turmeric and the split peas with 700 ml water and simmer 35 minutes.
Gomen: add the greens with a little water and cook 20 minutes; shiro: whisk the shiro powder into 500 ml water and simmer 15 minutes, seasoning each with salt.
Spoon each stew in mounds onto a large injera and serve with extra injera.
Sear the beef in the oil for 4 minutes and set aside.
Cook the onions in the butter for 8 minutes, add the garlic, berbere and tomato paste for 3 minutes.
Add 300 ml water and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return the beef and stir in the injera pieces until they soak up the sauce.
Boil the tripe for 30 minutes until tender and drain.
Melt the butter with the cardamom and fry the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the tripe and liver and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the minced beef, mitmita and jalapeños and cook for 4 minutes until done to your liking.
spiced with cardamom and fenugreek for niter kibbeh
Melt the butter gently with the cardamom.
Add the beef and mitmita and stir over low heat for 2 to 4 minutes until warmed through and cooked to medium (or longer for well done).
Serve with the fresh cheese and collard greens.
Soften the onions in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and turmeric for 2 minutes.
Add the potatoes, carrots and 400 ml water and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the chillies and salt and cook 5 minutes more.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with injera.
Cook the onions in a dry pot for 10 minutes until soft and darkening.
Add the oil, garlic, ginger, berbere, cardamom and tomato paste and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the lentils and water and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Rub the chicken with lemon juice and salt.
Cook the onions in a dry pot for 8 minutes, then add the oil and butter.
Add the garlic, ginger and turmeric for 2 minutes, then the chicken and 500 ml water.
Simmer covered for 30 minutes, add the potatoes and cook 20 minutes more.
Add the chillies, season and serve with injera.
Mix the berbere with lemon juice, one garlic clove and a little water to make awaze paste.
Sear the lamb in the oil for 4 minutes.
Add the onion, pepper, jalapeños and remaining garlic and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the butter and awaze and toss for 2 minutes.
Cook the onions in a dry pan for 5 minutes, then add the oil, garlic and tomato for 5 minutes.
Stir in the berbere, then whisk in the shiro powder with the water a little at a time.
Simmer, stirring, for 15 minutes until smooth and thick.
Toss the torn injera into the sauce until it soaks it up.
Marinate the fish with lemon juice, garlic, half the berbere and salt for 15 minutes.
Dust the fish with flour and fry in 3 tbsp oil for 5 minutes until crisp, then remove.
Fry the onion, pepper and jalapeños in the remaining oil for 4 minutes.
Add the tomato and remaining berbere for 2 minutes.
Return the fish, toss gently and serve with injera.
spiced with cardamom and fenugreek for niter kibbeh
Cook the onions in a dry pot for 8 minutes, then add the oil and butter.
Add the garlic, ginger and turmeric for 2 minutes.
Add the lamb and cook for 10 minutes, then 500 ml water, cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the potatoes and carrots for 20 minutes.
Add the chillies and salt and serve with injera.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and water into a thick batter.
Cook as two thick pancakes in a dry pan for 4 minutes per side.
Tear the pancakes into small pieces.
Melt the butter with the berbere and toss the pieces in it over low heat for 3 minutes.
Serve warm with honey and yogurt.
Rub the chicken with lemon juice and salt.
Cook the onions in a dry pot for 15 minutes, stirring, until soft and darkened, then add the butter.
Add the garlic, ginger, berbere and tomato paste and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the chicken and 500 ml water, cover and simmer for 40 minutes.
Add the eggs for 10 minutes and serve on injera.
Simmer the split peas in the water for 35 minutes until soft.
Cook the onions in a dry pan for 5 minutes, then add the oil and cook 5 minutes more.
Add the garlic, ginger and turmeric for 2 minutes.
Add the split peas with their liquid and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing slightly.
Add the chillies and salt and serve with injera.
Soak the wheat, barley and lentils overnight, then boil in 2 l water for 90 minutes until very soft.
Cook the beef with ginger garlic paste, spices, salt and half the oil, adding water as needed, for 2 hours until it shreds.
Add the beef to the grains and beat or blend briefly to a thick, stringy paste, cooking on low for 30 minutes.
Heat the remaining oil and pour over.
Serve with fried onions, lemon, herbs and ginger.
Tie the fennel, coriander, garlic and ginger in muslin and simmer with the chicken and salt in the water for 30 minutes to make yakhni, then remove the bag.
Fry the onions in the oil until golden, add the cumin, cloves, cinnamon and peppercorns.
Add the chicken and fry for 5 minutes.
Add the drained rice and 900 ml of the yakhni, boil until the water level drops below the rice.
Cover and cook on very low heat for 15 minutes.
nihari masala (fennel, ginger, chilli, long pepper)
Fry the beef in the oil with ginger garlic paste, spices and salt for 10 minutes.
Add 2 l water, cover and simmer on very low heat for 5 hours or overnight.
Whisk the atta into 200 ml water and stir in, cooking for 20 minutes until silky.
Taste and adjust the salt and chilli.
Serve with fried onions, ginger, chillies, coriander, lemon and naan.
Fry the onions in the oil for 10 minutes, add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and sear for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and spices and cook for 5 minutes.
Add 500 ml water, cover and simmer for 60 minutes until tender.
Blanch and purée the spinach with the green chillies.
Stir in the spinach and garam masala and cook uncovered for 10 minutes.
Fry the onions in the oil until golden, add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and sear for 10 minutes.
Add the yogurt, masala and salt with 500 ml water and simmer for 60 minutes until tender, then add the potatoes and plums.
Boil the rice for 6 minutes and drain.
Layer rice, mutton, tomatoes, chillies, mint and coriander in the pot.
Cover tightly and steam on low for 20 minutes.
Fry the cardamom in the ghee, add the chicken and ginger garlic paste and cook for 8 minutes without browning.
Add the onion purée, yogurt, white pepper and salt and cook for 15 minutes.
Stir in the cashew paste and 150 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cream and slit chillies and simmer 5 minutes.
Grind the soaked urad dal to a thick fluffy batter with salt and fry spoonfuls for 4 minutes until golden, then soak in warm water for 10 minutes and squeeze.
Whisk the yogurt with sugar, salt and a little water and soak the fritters in it.
Toss the chickpeas, potatoes, onion and tomatoes with chaat masala and tamarind chutney.
Arrange the chaat and dahi baray on plates.
Finish with cumin, coriander and extra chutney.
Fry the onions in the oil for 10 minutes, then sear the beef with the ginger garlic paste for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and spices and cook until the oil separates.
Add 800 ml water, cover and simmer for 75 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer 25 minutes until tender.
Sprinkle with garam masala and coriander and serve with roti.
Fry the okra in 2 tbsp oil for 8 minutes until it stops being sticky and remove.
Fry the cumin seeds in the remaining oil, add the onions for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and spices and cook 5 minutes.
Return the okra with salt and cook for 4 minutes.
Sprinkle with amchur and serve with roti.
Simmer the lentils in 1 l water with turmeric, chilli and tomato for 30 minutes until creamy.
Cook the rice in salted boiling water for 12 minutes and drain.
Heat the ghee and fry the cumin, garlic and dried chillies until the garlic is golden.
Pour the tempering over the dal and season.
Serve with the rice and coriander.
